To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the concentration of immunologic urinary kallikren in plasma does not always reflect alterations of immunoreactive kallikren excretion in urine.
plasma kallikreins do not correlate with renal kallikrin-kinins.
the concentration of iGKK does not correlate with the concentration of iUKK in plasma and that the concentration of GKK in plasma does not correlate with urinary kallikren excretion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of renal and plasma kallikreins.
the role of the kallikreins in blood pressure regulation.
the regulation of the renin-angiotensin system and the kallikreinkinin system in the kidney.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the plasma glandular kallkrein is not a reliable index of urinary kallkrein excretion.
there is an association of iGKK with iUKK during low sodium intake, but not in the other experimental conditions.
the plasma level of iGK is not a reliable indicator of the activity and/or concentration of iGK in the kidney.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the concentration of iGKK and iUKK in plasma are not necessarily parallel, and that iUKK cannot be used as an index of iGKK concentration in plasma.
urinary kallkrein is not a reliable indicator of the activity in the systemic circulation of the renal kinnikrein system.
the concentration of iGKK is a more reliable index of renal kallikren-kinin system activity than iUKK.
The main takeaway from our work is that
urinary kallkirein excretion cannot always be used as an indicator of renal kallikren-kinin system activity.

the concentration of kallikreins in the circulation is regulated by a complex set of factors and that the concentration of immunologic kallikreines does not necessarily parallel the concentration of active kallikreine.

the concentration of kallikreins in plasma does not parallel the urinary kallikren excretion, and therefore, urinary kallikrin excretion is not an indicator of the kallikrin-kinin system activity in systemic circulation.
